lectures.title: Why Bellman Ford Catches Negative Cycle in Vth Iteration?

cues.en: Now the question is why?
Bellman-ford algorithm catch the negative cycle in v4 iteration.
Why not before?
Now, to answer this question, let's first identify why Bellman-ford algorithm runs v minus one times.
Now we know that Bellman-ford algorithm tries to see if any node achieved a better distance in the previous
iteration.
So if a better distance is achieved in the previous iteration, in the current step, it tries to use
that and improve the distance of other vertices.
It means that initially we said that apart from the source vertex, all other vertices to set the infinity,
and in each step it uses better distance to improve the other distances.
Now it's obvious that if the graph has five vertices, the maximum number of the edge to travel from
source to any given destination is going to be four.
It takes four edges to reach any vertex from the beginning vertex.
Now, in our case, in this graph, to go to any other vertices, it takes 2 or 3 steps because our
graph is not a worst case graph.
Now if we arrange this graph like this.

it takes four steps over here.
Now in our case we have five elements over here.
But it takes four steps.

In case of Bellman-ford algorithm.

Now in case of this graph, if we do do so, you will see that in the first iteration it's going to

So that's why Bellman-ford algorithm catches the negative cycle in fifth iteration.
